newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE EUROYEN ENDS FLAT IN DIRECTIONLESS TRADE.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE EUROYEN ENDS FLAT IN DIRECTIONLESS TRADE.

text.p: Key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures closed unchanged on Tuesday after staying within the recent range in the middle of Japan's "Obon" summer holiday season.
Traders said operators were getting cautious about buying further after the contract hit a short-term ceiling. It stopped rising at 99.24 on Monday despite sharp falls in Tokyo stocks.
Meanwhile, the downside was supported at 99.20, they said.
The March settled at 99.22 after moving between 99.20 and 99.23. Turnover was 38,162 contracts.

"The recovery in Tokyo stocks prompted light selling but the March contract was firmly underpinned at 99.20 due to a lack of fresh factors," said dealer at a long-term credit bank. "March will remain more sensitive to bearish factors (than bullish ones) in coming weeks as its topside looks heavy."

Traders said the contract was facing a stiff ceiling, partly because three-month cash interest rates had stopped falling recently. There were also increasing fears that the government may move to prop up stock prices, they said.
"The benchmark three-month CD rate recently fell as low as 0.58 percent. But it is unlikely investors will agree to buy CDs with lower rates," a city bank dealer said.
Another market concern was that U.S. Treasuries and stocks could tumble again this week, when no major domestic economic data is due, traders said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) conducted a neutral money market operation in the morning for a fourth day in a row. The operation was in line with market expectations, traders said.
The key overnight call rate was mainly traded at 0.47 percent, unchanged from Monday's weighted average.
About 20 billion yen of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.58 percent, which was steady from Monday and the lowest rate since May 23.

Some 30 billion yen of two-month CDs were issued at 0.59 percent. The rate was higher due to technical demand from issuers for CDs which mature sooner than three-month CDs after end-September half-year book closings, traders said.

In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, light selling was seen from banks in line with weakness in yen bonds. The five-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.80/1.84 percent against Monday's 1.77/1.81 percent.
